title: Effective descent of etale spaces along one surjective etale cover
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention], and let $M,U$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $a:U\to M$ be a surjective etale morphism and $v:V\to U$ an etale morphism of algebraic spaces. Etale means etale on scheme charts [def-weil-etale-morphism]; surjective means onto field-valued point classes. Put $U_2=U\times_MU$ and $U_3=U\times_MU\times_MU$, using sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Suppose an isomorphism $\theta:p_1^*V\xrightarrow{\sim}p_2^*V$ over $U_2$ restricts to the identity over the diagonal $U\to U_2$ and satisfies $p_{23}^*\theta\circ p_{12}^*\theta=p_{13}^*\theta$ over $U_3$. Then there exist an algebraic space $N/S$, an etale map $N\to M$, and an isomorphism $N\times_MU\simeq V$ over $U$ whose induced overlap isomorphism is $\theta$. For any two etale algebraic spaces over $M$, pullback along $a$ gives a bijection between morphisms over $M$ and morphisms over $U$ respecting their canonical overlap isomorphisms. Thus a realization of $(V,\theta)$ is unique up to unique isomorphism compatible with its displayed identification. No quasi-compactness or finite-type hypothesis is imposed on $a$ or $v$.

source.place: Tag 0ADV (lemma-descend-algebraic-space), part (1) for the singleton covering {U -> M}; spaces-descent.tex Tag 0ADT (lemma-descent-data-sheaves) for full faithfulness, and Tag 042B (lemma-descending-property-etale) for etaleness of the descended map.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], the etale map $a$ is flat and locally of finite presentation; its surjectivity is part of the hypotheses. Thus the singleton $\{a\}$ is an fppf covering in the explicit sense of [lem-sfb-fppf-space-datum-sheaf-realization]. The given $\theta$ supplies its descent datum: the two local copies of $V$ are over the ordered two factors of $U_2$, and the stated equation on $U_3$ is precisely its cocycle.

Apply [lem-sfb-fppf-space-datum-sheaf-realization] to obtain an fppf sheaf $F\to M$ and $e:F\times_M U\xrightarrow{\sim}V$ over $U$ inducing $\theta$. Write $q:V\to F$ for the projection $F\times_M U\to F$ composed with $e^{-1}$. At this point $F$ is only a sheaf; no effectivity as an algebraic space has been used.

source.place: Tag 0ADT (lemma-descent-data-sheaves), functor from descent data to sheaves and its equivalence.

proof.text: For an $S$-scheme $T$ and $x\in F(T)$, fibre-product associativity gives $h_T\times_{x,F,q}V\simeq h_T\times_M U$: a section on the left is $(t,v)$ with $q(v)=x(t)$, and $e^{-1}(v)=(x(t),u)$ sends it to $(t,u)$; conversely $(t,u)$ gives $v=e(x(t),u)$. These are natural inverse maps. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], the right side is an algebraic space and its map to $T$ is surjective etale. By [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] this map is flat and locally of finite presentation. Thus $q$ satisfies every scheme-test hypothesis of [lem-sfb-fppf-space-atlas-bootstrap], with atlas space $V$. That node proves $F$ is an algebraic space. Set $N=F$.

The morphism $N\to M$ pulls back along $a$ to $V\to U$, which is etale by hypothesis. Apply the algebraic-space, etale clause of [lem-sfb-representable-fppf-etale-open-descent], using flatness, local finite presentation and surjectivity of $a$ verified in step 1. It follows that $N\to M$ is etale. The isomorphism $e:N\times_MU\simeq V$ still induces $\theta$, since neither the underlying sheaf nor $e$ was changed.

source.place: Tag 042B (lemma-descending-property-etale); target locality applied to the singleton fppf covering.

proof.text: For etale spaces $N_1,N_2$ over $M$, their underlying sheaves lie in $\mathcal L$ of [lem-sfb-fppf-space-datum-sheaf-realization]: the local pullbacks are algebraic spaces by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Its full faithfulness gives exactly the claimed bijection of maps, since morphisms of algebraic spaces are natural transformations [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For two realizations, the displayed identifications with $V$ give inverse compatible local isomorphisms. Descend both by the bijection. Their composites are identities because their pullbacks are identities and the bijection is injective. This gives the unique isomorphism compatible with the displays. No step required quasi-compactness or finite type; in particular the use of the bootstrap involved a single atlas space, not an unbounded coproduct.

source.place: Tag 0ADT (lemma-descent-data-sheaves), functor from descent data to sheaves and its equivalence.
